findings.claim: the soldier who “unseam’d” the rebel Macdonwald “from the nave to the chaps.”
findings.truth: The line reads “from the nave to the chops”. Lesson 6 already quotes it correctly, so the unit contradicts itself.
findings.evidence: Gutenberg Macbeth 1.2: 'Till he unseam’d him from the nave to the chops,'

findings.claim: James claimed to be descended from the real-life Banquo (repeated in flashcard 3).
findings.truth: Banquo is not a documented historical person. He appears in the Scottish chronicle tradition (Boece, then Holinshed) as a Stuart ancestor. The Stuart claim of descent is real; 'the real-life Banquo' is not. Dropping 'real-life' keeps the point and removes the false claim.
findings.evidence: Holinshed's Chronicles (1587) is the source; no contemporary record of Banquo exists.

findings.claim: Literal spec code 'OCR J352' appears 18 times across lessons 2-8 (L2 ×1, L3 ×2, L4 ×2, L5 ×2, L6 ×2, L7 ×4, L8 ×5), and 'Component 02' once in a lesson 8 knowledge check.
findings.truth: Both are banned strings in the house validator. Each one is replaced with board-neutral wording ('the extract question', 'the Shakespeare question', 'the poetry and Shakespeare paper'). No claim of fact changes.
findings.evidence: CHECK_PROMPT.md banned-strings list; the previous OCR Shakespeare unit carried the same 16-plus strings.

findings.claim: Lesson 4 description is 100 characters; lesson 7 description is 101 characters.
findings.truth: The validator requires under 100 characters. Both trimmed without loss of meaning.

findings.claim: Three sentences end with an AO code and a full stop ('...important for AO2.', '...confident AO2.', '...top-band AO2.').
findings.truth: The validator rejects an AO code immediately followed by a full stop. One word added after each code.

findings.claim: You have roughly 45 minutes for the Shakespeare question. Spend 5 minutes planning, 35 minutes writing, and 5 minutes checking SPaG (AO4).
findings.truth: The poetry and Shakespeare paper is 2 hours for 80 marks, 40 marks for Section A and 40 marks for Section B. The Shakespeare question is therefore worth about an hour, not 45 minutes. Advising 45 minutes would cost a student a quarter of the writing time. Rewritten as an hour: 10 minutes planning, 45 writing, 5 checking.
findings.evidence: specs/ocr/english-literature-J352.md, component summary: 'Exploring poetry and Shakespeare (02) ... closed text, 2 hour examination worth 80 marks: 40 marks for Section A and 40 marks for Section B.'

findings.claim: 'In the OCR J352 Component 02 Shakespeare question, how many marks is each question worth?'
findings.truth: Two banned spec codes, and 'each question' misleads: Section B sets ONE extended response, chosen from two options. The stem is rewritten board-neutrally; the keyed answer (40 marks) is correct and unchanged. The same spec code is stripped from practice question 6 in the same lesson.
findings.evidence: spec component summary: 'Learners respond to one extended response-style question on their studied play, from a choice of two'.

findings.claim: Why might Shakespeare's description of Macbeth as a 'dead butcher' be seen as inadequate?
findings.truth: 'This dead butcher, and his fiend-like queen' is Malcolm's line in the closing speech, not Shakespeare speaking. The question's own first half already names Malcolm's speech, so the attribution contradicts itself.
findings.evidence: Gutenberg Macbeth 5.8: MALCOLM. '...this dead butcher, and his fiend-like queen'.

findings.claim: Match option: "Macbeth echoes 'fair and foul' before meeting the witches".
findings.truth: Macbeth's line is 'So foul and fair a day I have not seen' (1.3). The lesson body quotes it correctly; only the match option reverses the pair.
findings.evidence: Gutenberg Macbeth 1.3: 'So foul and fair a day I have not seen.'

findings.claim: 21 practice questions across lessons 2-8 are typed '4 marks — Quote Analysis' while their band ladder runs 'Top band (7-8) / Upper-mid band (5-6) / Lower-mid band (3-4) / Lower band (1-2)'.
findings.truth: The label and the ladder contradict each other. The band descriptors are sized for an 8-mark answer (three moments, several quotations), so the ladder is right and the label is wrong. Type relabelled to '8 marks — Quote Analysis' on all 21.
findings.evidence: Every affected question carries the identical 8-mark ladder; the template default '4 marks' never matches it.

findings.claim: All six lesson 1 ladders use 'Mastering / Secure / Developing / Emerging' with no mark ranges at all.
findings.truth: A student cannot calibrate an answer against a ladder that carries no marks, and the band names are not the house ladder. Rescaled to five equal house bands across the real 40-mark total: Top (33-40), Upper-mid (25-32), Mid (17-24), Lower-mid (9-16), Low (1-8). Existing descriptors preserved in order.
findings.evidence: Section B is a single 40-mark extended response (spec component summary).

findings.claim: The unit's practice bank mixes 40-mark essay questions with 21 short 'Quote Analysis' items.
findings.truth: Section B of the poetry and Shakespeare paper sets exactly one 40-mark extended response, from a choice of two (extract-based with links to the whole play, OR discursive). There is no short-answer Shakespeare question on the paper. Two defensible options: (a) keep the short items as skills drills, now honestly labelled 8 marks (what I have done); or (b) rebuild all 21 as 40-mark extract or discursive questions so every practice item mirrors the real paper. Option (b) is a rewrite, not a surgical fix, so I have not attempted it. ORCHESTRATOR: left for the relabel / band-ladder workstream (marks correct; drills kept).
findings.evidence: specs/ocr/english-literature-J352.md, Section B: Shakespeare (25% of total GCSE), one extended response from a choice of two.

findings.claim: The 21 forty-mark ladders in lessons 2-8 use six bands (Top / Upper / Upper-mid / Mid / Lower-mid / Lower) rather than the five house bands.
findings.truth: The mark ranges are correct and total 40, and none of the band names is a banned string, so I left them rather than rewrite 21 mark schemes for style. If you want the unit internally consistent with the five-band ladder I applied to lesson 1, say so and I will normalise all 21 in one pass. ORCHESTRATOR: left for the relabel / band-ladder workstream (marks correct; drills kept).
findings.evidence: CHECK_PROMPT.md house ladder: Top / Upper-mid / Mid / Lower-mid / Low / Basic.

findings.claim: 'hamartia' is listed twice in the lesson 2 glossary, with two slightly different definitions.
findings.truth: Both definitions are correct, so nothing is factually wrong; the entry is simply duplicated. Removing an array item is outside the surgical-edit shape, so I have left it.

findings.claim: In the paragraph on Act 3 Scene 3: 'The first murderer reports: Fleance is 'scaped.'
findings.truth: The murderer makes that report to Macbeth at the banquet in Act 3 Scene 4, not during the ambush in 3.3. The paragraph never states the wrong scene outright, so a student is unlikely to be marked down, but the placement invites the error.

summary: One HIGH error: lesson 8 tells students the Shakespeare question is worth 45 minutes when the paper gives 2 hours for two 40-mark sections, so it is worth about an hour. Every quotation in all eight lessons checks out against the Gutenberg text for wording, speaker and act.scene, with one word wrong ('chaps' for 'chops') and one paradox reversed in a match option; the rest of the yield is the banned 'OCR J352' spec code 18 times, two mark-label or ladder inconsistencies, and validator-limit trims.
